Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 6–7:

ومن الناس من یشتری ۔۔۔۔۔ فبشرہ بعذاب الیم (6 – 7)

By "lahw al-hadith" (idle talk) is meant entertaining and amusing speech, the kind which is desired only to pass the time. Such speech yields no good or beneficial result, nor does it contain any constructive matter related to the station of man as God's vicegerent (khilafah). It is not tied to any mental, moral, economic, religious or otherworldly purpose. Islam assigns to man certain duties in this world, and it also determines the limits, means and methods of carrying out those duties. This verse is general. It presents a type of person who is commonly found in every time and place. Some narrations indicate that in the era of the first community of Islam a specific incident took place, and this verse alludes to it. Nadr ibn al-Harith, a literary figure of Mecca, used to buy books from Iran containing the tales and historical accounts of the Iranians and their great men, and the amusing stories of their wars. This man would sit in the lanes of Mecca and stop those who were going to listen to the Qur'an, and would recount these tales to them. He used to narrate the stories of Iran in opposition to the stories of the Qur'an (qasas al-Qur'an). Even if it is established that this verse was revealed in connection with that incident, the verse is still general. It clearly describes the characteristics of this kind of people. Such people are found in every age. They were present in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also, in the period when this verse was revealed in Mecca.

﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾ (31:6). That is, he spends his wealth and his time on it, and exhausts his life in it. He spends such precious things on such worthless and valueless things. He consumes his limited and precious life in it, a life which neither returns nor can be brought back. Why does he do this?

﴿to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge and to take it in ridicule﴾ (31:6). That is, he misleads people from the path of Allah without knowledge, and mocks the call to that path. Such a person is ignorant, and reality is hidden from his sight. He does nothing on the basis of knowledge and certainty. Nor does he act on the basis of wisdom. His intention is corrupt and his purpose is perverse. He wants to lead people astray. He misguides himself and also misguides others, and wastes his life uselessly in this. Then he is so audacious that he mocks the Islamic call and mocks the Islamic system which Allah has ordained so that it may be the constitution of people's lives. Therefore the Qur'an, even before portraying such people, threatens them with humiliating punishment.

﴿For those will be a humiliating punishment﴾ (31:6). A severely humiliating punishment is for such people, because they attempted to disgrace the Islamic call here. These people used to make a jest of the Islamic way of life. Now, after this threat, the features of this group are inscribed.

﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them﴾ (31:7). This is a scene in which the conduct of this arrogant person is vividly portrayed. He turns away with great pride and passes by, pretending not to hear. Then the next colour in this picture is filled with utmost contempt.

﴿as though there was in his ears deafness﴾ (31:7). As if the heaviness of his ears prevents the verses of Allah from reaching them. Otherwise, if any human being were to hear these verses, he could not treat them with this contemptible behaviour. This colour is then made even more humiliating.

﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (31:7). This is not an occasion for good tidings, but here their humiliation is intended, and this manner is appropriate for such arrogant mockers.

In view of the humiliating punishment for those who turn away, act arrogantly and disbelieve, it is necessary here to also mention the reward of the righteous believers who do good deeds. Their mention was made at the beginning of this Surah, and their success was stated there, although it was there in summary form.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 8–9:

Wherever the Qur'an mentions the reward of the believers, it always mentions righteous deeds (ʿamal ṣāliḥ) alongside faith. This is because the temperament of the Islamic outlook on life does not allow faith to be a frozen, hidden, inactive and abstract idea. Rather, faith must be a living, active and dynamic reality. When it is born in the heart, takes root and is complete, it must become dynamic and take practical form. It must take the shape of movement and conduct, and its effects must speak for it in the realm of reality, so that it can be known what is in the heart of this believer. These are the people who believed and gave practical form to their faith.

﴿لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ النَّعِيمِ﴾ (31:8) "For them are Gardens of Bliss, wherein they will abide."  These gardens and this permanence are being given to them according to the promise of Allah.

﴿وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ (31:9) "It is the true promise of Allah." The mercy of Allah has advanced to such a degree that He has made it binding upon Himself to show kindness to His servants. **Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 10–11:**

Khalaqa as-samawati bi-ghayri … fi dalalin mubin (10–11)

These heavens, without our presenting the complex modern scientific information about them, when they come before our senses in their outward state, appear very great. Whether these heavens are the stars and planets, or the galaxies and nebulae, which float in the heights, and only Allah knows their true secret; or whether the heaven means this dome which we see, whose reality only Allah is aware of: whatever is meant by the heaven, in any case these great spheres stand without support or pillars.人 (humans) see these heavens night and day, and the distances we bring close from the small star upon which man rides, the mere imagining of this universe turns the head, that this world is so vast and terrifying, whose limits and boundaries are still beyond human comprehension. Then when a person thinks that this great universe has been bound into an organized system, such that in its movement there is not even a difference of one second, then how beautifully this world has been made, so that a person keeps looking and the heart keeps thinking and does not tire, the eyes keep gazing and are not satiated with its sight. And when a person thinks that among the tiny points visible in this round sky, each single star is thousands of times larger than the earth (for example Jupiter is a thousand times larger), even millions of times larger, then for any intelligent person this is sufficient proof. Let us return from this endless journey through the space of the universe; the Qur'an has only made a passing allusion to it.

*Khalaqa as-samawati bi-ghayri 'amadin tarawnaha* (31:10): "He created the heavens without pillars that you can see." Now, turn to this very earth, and look at its sights closely and for a long time. This small earth, a particle of the universe, in that great universe is indeed only a particle floating in space. We come back to it. We think that this earth is very vast and extensive; man cannot even tour it in his short life, even if he spends his whole life wandering this small dust-mote. Man is told: just study this with open eyes, and because of long familiarity and repeated viewing, its wondrousness has disappeared from man. Look at its marvels.

*Wa-alqa fil-ardi rawasiya an tamida bikum* (31:10): "And He placed firm mountains in the earth so that it would not tilt and carry you away." *Rawasi* means mountains. The scholars of geology say that mountains are in fact the wrinkles of the earth's crust. When the crust of the earth cooled and the gases within it contracted, the volume of the earth decreased, as a result of which wrinkles were produced in the crust of the earth, and thus heights, depths and undulations arose upon the earth. Wherever there was more contraction, the mountains rose higher. Now, whether the theory of the geologists is correct or incorrect, the Book of Allah says this: Allah placed mountains so that there would be balance in the movement of the earth, and man could stand firm on its surface, and there would be no swaying within it. The theory of the geologists may be correct, and they themselves accept that if there were no mountains, the rotational motion of the earth would not have the balance that it has; and the command of Allah is exalted in every state and will remain so, because Allah is the most truthful of all speakers. *Sadaqa Allahu al-'Azim.*

*Wa-bassa fiha min kulli dabbatin* (31:10): "And He spread throughout it creatures of every kind." Among the wonders of this great universe, this is an astonishing marvel: that Allah has spread out colourful life upon this earth. Until today no one has been able to discover the secret of life itself, let alone its variety and diversity. Man has not even been able to grasp the simplest form of this life, much less to know the higher kinds of life, their variety and their different sizes, and beautiful animals and birds, whose number man does not even know. It is very regrettable that some people, despite knowledge, pass by these wonders with eyes closed, as though they were looking at something quite ordinary. This same human, when he sees a small machine made by man, is amazed and keeps turning it over and over and looking at it, although this machine cannot be more complex than a simple cell created by Allah; and the subtle and complicated functions of these cells are all marvels. We are speaking only of the marvels of the simple cell. As for those large beings of complex creation, in whose bodies hundreds of chemical laboratories and workshops are functioning, within which are hundreds of stores where materials are gathered and distributed, and within which there is a wondrous communication system that receives and sends messages as wireless signals, and hundreds of other processes carry out thousands of duties.

*Wa-anzalna min … zawjin karim* (31:10): "And We sent down water from the heavens and caused every noble kind of plant to grow in the earth." The sending down of water from the heavens is one of the marvels of creation; but because it is often repeated before our eyes, we pass over it with heedlessness. This water, through which rivers flow, by which seas are filled, with which springs gush forth in the earth. This water descends from the heavens under an extremely intricate system. It is linked with the system of the heavens; its nature, its composition, and its relation to the distances of the spheres are all connected. Then, after the descent of water, within the earth there arise plants of many kinds and many forms, with different tastes, different colours, different sizes, and different properties. Their wonders are such that they never seem to end: the life and growth in plants, their variety, and the hereditary characteristics present within a tiny seed. This small seed reproduces itself; it takes the form of a plant, a flower and a tree. Merely studying the distribution of colours within a single flower draws a person towards the great powers of the Creator of the universe, and a person's faith keeps growing deeper.

Then the Qur'an clarifies that Allah also created pairs among plants.

*Min kulli zawjin karim* (31:10): "Of every noble pair." This is the great truth which science has come to know and experience only in quite recent times. In every plant there are male and female cells. These cells are found within one flower, or in two flowers of one branch, or these cells are separately located in two trees; and no plant bears fruit until the male and female cells unite, just as the reproductive system of humans and animals is evident. And the attribute *karim* ("noble") alongside *zawj* ("pair"): through the use of this word a particular impression is intended, that this is the creation of the Noble Allah, and that it is a very important marvel which should be viewed with the eye of reflection and respected. It has been brought in also so that, since Allah has done these noble works, you should tell us what those beings you have taken as gods have done. This is:

*Hadha khalqu … min dunihi* (31:11): "This is the creation of Allah; now show me what those others besides Him have created." After "every noble pair," this is the challenge; and now this is the conclusion:

*Bal az-zalimuna fi dalalin mubin* (31:11): "Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error." And what greater wrong can there be than shirk, when this marvel of the great universe is before us? Here the first journey ends, and it concludes with words of great finality.

After this, the second round now begins. It is in an entirely new arrangement. It is indirect guidance and a narrative style of admonition. The subject under discussion is giving thanks to Allah alone, and declaring Allah free from every kind of shirk. Within this narrative, the matter of the Hereafter, deeds and their recompense is mentioned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verse 12:

ولقد اتینا لقمن ۔۔۔۔ غنی حمید (12)

Here, through the words of Luqman the Wise (Hakim), the doctrine of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah), the doctrine of the Hereafter (Akhirah), and other moral teachings are given. Opinions about him differ. Some say he was a Prophet, while others say that without the office of prophethood he was a righteous servant (abd salih). Most commentators have adopted this second view. Some say that he was an Abyssinian slave. Some have also said that he was from Nubia. Some have said that he was one of the judges of the Children of Israel. Whatever he was, the Quran has informed us that he was a person to whom Allah had granted wisdom (hikmah), and the essence of this wisdom and philosophy was that Allah should be thanked.

ولقد اتینا ۔۔۔۔ اشکر للہ (31: 12) "We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Be grateful to Allah." Thus, in the course of this account, the Quran guides us to give thanks to Allah, and along with this guidance and information, that gratitude is a store of benefit for the one who gives thanks. Its benefit returns to the grateful person himself, because Allah is the Self-Sufficient King; whether someone gives thanks or not, His sovereignty is not affected. Allah is inherently Praiseworthy (Hamid), whether or not anyone praises Him.

ومن یشکر۔۔۔۔۔ غنی حمید (31: 12) "Whoever gives thanks, his thanks benefit only himself; and whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy." Therefore, he is a great fool who opposes wisdom and does not gather this treasure for himself.

Now the issue of Tawhid is presented through an address that Luqman gave to his son.

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ ۔۔۔۔۔ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ (13)

This is an advice that is free from every kind of doubt, because no father can intend anything for his son except good. A father can only be a sincere and compassionate adviser to his son. These are the words of Luqman the wise, who forbids his son from associating partners with Allah (shirk) and gives this reason: that shirk is in fact a great wrong. In his speech he repeats this point twice. The first time, he forbids shirk and states its reason. The second time, he emphasizes it with the particle "inna" (indeed) and the emphatic lam (lam al-ta'kid). This is the same matter that Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) presents before his people, yet they dispute without any basis. Because he insists on this belief, they level accusations against him, suggesting that perhaps he has some personal aim behind it, such as wanting to become a ruler and to rise above them as a great man. Therefore, their claim is not correct, because Hazrat Luqman delivers this very same speech to his son and commands him to refrain from shirk. It is obvious that a father cannot, at the very least, say anything wrong to his son. Hence, this advice is free from every kind of suspicion and conjecture. The truth is that everyone who is granted wisdom holds the belief in the Oneness of Allah (tawhid). There is nothing but good in the belief in tawhid, and this is a psychological argument.

Since this was a compassionate advice from a father to his son, it is also made clear that when a father is so sincere and compassionate towards his children, all people are commanded that they have a right upon you, namely that of their parents. This discourse is also in the most affectionate words. The relationship between father and son, parents and children, is described here in a very tender and suggestive manner. Yet, despite this, the relationship of belief and ideological connection is given precedence over the ties of lineage and blood.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 14–15:

﴿We have enjoined upon man (kindness) to his parents...﴾ to ﴿...of what you used to do﴾ (14–15)

The Qur'an repeatedly admonishes children to look after their parents, and the sayings of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also emphasize this again and again. In contrast, very little guidance has been given to parents regarding their children. The only admonition given concerns the wicked custom of burying infant daughters alive, and that practice existed only in very limited areas. The reason is that compassion and tenderness toward children are instilled deeply in the nature of every human being. In order to keep the chain of life continuing, Allah has placed in parents the inner impulse to care for their children. Parents spend their bodies, their nerves and their lives for their children. They sacrifice their every precious possession for them, and in the path of this they do not utter "uff" when faced with any hardship, nor do they complain. Rather, at times parents do everything for their children unconsciously, and indeed they sacrifice everything for them with great joy. In this way, it is as though parents do all of this for themselves. Therefore, human nature is self-sufficient with regard to children; there is no need for any further exhortation or emphasis. As for children and offspring, they need to be repeatedly reminded that they should take care of that generation which has sacrificed everything for them, which made every effort for them, and whose dreams are like flickering lamps or the lamps of dawn, who have distilled their age, their bodies and their spirits to prepare the provision of your life. As far as children and offspring are concerned, they cannot repay the full recompense of their parents' sacrifices, even if they devote their entire lives to them. Just look at this impactful verse.

﴿His mother bore him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years﴾ (31:14). No more beautiful picture of this sacrifice and this goodness can be drawn. By her natural duty, the mother gives more sacrifice, and her love, affection and gentleness toward children are greater than those of the father. Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar (a hadith compiler) has narrated in his chain of transmission, through Buraydah, that a man was in the circumambulation (tawaf), carrying his mother on his back and making her perform the tawaf, and he asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Have I fulfilled her right?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No, not even for a single breath. Indeed, not even for a single breath." This refers to the period of pregnancy and the period of childbirth, when she bore him in weakness upon weakness. In the shade of this pleasant gratitude, attention is drawn to the fact that it is also necessary to be grateful to the first Benefactor. The first gratitude is due to Allah, and the second is due to the parents.

﴿That give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾ (31:14). And along with these realities, remember this important truth as well: ﴿To Me is the final destination﴾ (31:14). And there, only this provision will benefit you.

However, despite this emphasized bond between parents and children, and despite the honor and respect that children must show, this relationship is secondary. Before it comes the ideological bond. Therefore, children must also remember that, in matters of belief, even the commands and desires of parents may be rejected.

﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾ (31:15). Because the boundary of obedience to parents ends here. Beyond this is the command to obey the Lord, and the ideological bond is superior and higher than the bond between father and son. Therefore, whatever commands parents may give to make someone a associator (mushrik), whatever efforts they make, whatever pressure they apply, whatever demands they make, and even if they become angry, such instructions cannot be obeyed, because a child does not know that Allah has any partner. Therefore, the command is that beyond this point there is no obedience to parents; there is obedience to the Creator.

However, despite the command of disobedience to parents in ideological disagreement and in matters of belief, the respect and honor due to parents and kindness toward them remain necessary.

﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ (31:15). This worldly life is but a brief journey; the real journey is that.

﴿And follow the way of one who turns to Me in repentance﴾ (31:15). That is, follow the believers. And after this brief journey, you must present yourselves before Allah.

﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ (31:15). Then all of you must return to Me, and then I will tell you how you acted. And for every person there will be recompense there for their deeds, whether they were grateful or ungrateful, whether they adopted the path of shirk or embraced the way of tawhid.

It is related in narrations that this verse, the verse in Surah al-'Ankabut that is similar to it, and a verse in Surah al-Ahqaf that has the same theme, were revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) and his mother. (I have given the details in the context of the verse of Surah al-'Ankabut in the twentieth juz'.) Some narrations state that this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Malik (RA). Tabarani has quoted it in *Kitab al-'Ashrah*, narrating it from Dawud ibn Basil. The story of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas appears in a hadith of Muslim, and that is the more preponderant view; however, the meaning and the ruling will be general for all such circumstances. The point is that in relationships there are also degrees, and in obligations there are also degrees. Every command and every relationship has its own value and worth. Therefore, in Islam, the connection with Allah is the first connection, and the rights of Allah hold the highest rank. The Qur'an repeatedly points out this order of ranks, so that if the distinction of ranks were not made, ... And emphasis is repeated so that there remains no ambiguity or confusion in this matter.

This was a parenthetical digression (*jumla mu'tarizah*) within the speech of Luqman. After this, his discourse and advice resume. And this matter concerns resurrection after death, gathering and reckoning, and reward and punishment: that there everyone will receive reward and punishment, and this will be most just. However, this principle is not presented merely as an abstract principle, but is presented in the form of a cosmic parable and image, in such an impactful manner that human consciousness is deeply affected. In this image it is explained that Allah knows every particle of this universe, and therefore He is able to bring together all the particles of every person's body.

Therefore, whatever commands parents may give to make someone a associator (mushrik), whatever efforts they make, whatever pressure they apply, whatever demands they make, and even if they become angry, such instructions cannot be obeyed, because a child does not know that Allah has any partner. Therefore, the command is that beyond this point there is no obedience to parents; there is obedience to the Creator.

However, despite the command of disobedience to parents in ideological disagreement and in matters of belief, the respect and honor due to parents and kindness toward them remain necessary.

﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ (31:15). This worldly life is but a brief journey; the real journey is that.

﴿And follow the way of one who turns to Me in repentance﴾ (31:15). That is, follow the believers. And after this brief journey, you must present yourselves before Allah.

﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ (31:15). Then all of you must return to Me, and then I will tell you how you acted. And for every person there will be recompense there for their deeds, whether they were grateful or ungrateful, whether they adopted the path of shirk or embraced the way of tawhid.

It is related in narrations that this verse, the verse in Surah al-'Ankabut that is similar to it, and a verse in Surah al-Ahqaf that has the same theme, were revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) and his mother. (I have given the details in the context of the verse of Surah al-'Ankabut in the twentieth juz'.) Some narrations state that this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Malik (RA). Tabarani has quoted it in *Kitab al-'Ashrah*, narrating it from Dawud ibn Basil. The story of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas appears in a hadith of Muslim, and that is the more preponderant view; however, the meaning and the ruling will be general for all such circumstances. The point is that in relationships there are also degrees, and in obligations there are also degrees. Every command and every relationship has its own value and worth. Therefore, in Islam, the connection with Allah is the first connection, and the rights of Allah hold the highest rank. The Qur'an repeatedly points out this order of ranks, so that if the distinction of ranks were not made, ... And emphasis is repeated so that there remains no ambiguity or confusion in this matter.

This was a parenthetical digression (*jumla mu'tarizah*) within the speech of Luqman. After this, his discourse and advice resume. And this matter concerns resurrection after death, gathering and reckoning, and reward and punishment: that there everyone will receive reward and punishment, and this will be most just. However, this principle is not presented merely as an abstract principle, but is presented in the form of a cosmic parable and image, in such an impactful manner that human consciousness is deeply affected. In this image it is explained that Allah knows every particle of this universe, and therefore He is able to bring together all the particles of every person's body.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verse 16:

﴿Yā bunayya innahā in ... inna Allāha Laṭīfun Khabīr﴾ (16)

If someone were to describe the all-encompassing and all-penetrating nature of Allah's knowledge merely in abstract terms, saying that Allah has power over everything and that He takes account of every atom, such a statement would not be nearly as forceful and striking as this vivid manner of expression. This is the distinctive style of the Qur'an: it renders matters that are highly abstract and mental into images that can be seen. (See my book al-Taswir al-Fanni fi'l-Qur'an.)

A grain of mustard seed is very small, lost, insignificant and weightless. It has no value. Now, whether this grain is inside a rock (ṣakhra), to which there is no path, or in the heavens, whose vast distances make one's head spin, where enormous bodies of celestial spheres float in their weight, or whether it lies somewhere in the earth, buried in dust, He will bring it out. So consider, then, His knowledge and power. He is extremely subtle in His perception.

The word al-Latif fits perfectly with this theme: ﴿Inna Allaha Latifun Khabir﴾ (31:16). The mind races through the valleys of this terrifying, vast and boundless universe in pursuit of that grain of mustard seed, and it fails to encompass the reach of Allah's knowledge and power. So it turns back to Allah, acknowledges its own helplessness, and believes that Allah knows every hidden thing. That realization settles in the mind, and it is the very thing the entire Qur'an seeks to fix in the human heart: that "He" is watching. These are most excellent and captivating methods of expression.

Luqman continues advising his son. Having firmly established faith in Allah, eliminated every trace of shirk from the heart, affirmed belief in the Hereafter and instilled the Islamic worldview in the heart, he now presents the demands of Islamic belief. These demands are: to establish prayer (salah) in order to maintain connection with Allah, which is the ascension (mi'raj) of the believer; and to call people to Islam in order to maintain connection with them. Whoever calls others to the truth faces hardships, so be patient over those hardships.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verse 17:

"O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently whatever befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination." (Qur'an 31:17)

This is the path of the Islamic worldview: to regard Allah as One without partner, to cultivate the awareness that He is watching, to desire that the real reward is with Him, to trust that He will act justly, and to fear His punishment at all times. After this, one calls people to Allah, reforms them, enjoins what is right (ma'ruf) and forbids what is wrong (munkar). And before all these matters, one must prepare oneself for confrontation with kufr. In this path, moral preparation is more important than material preparation. And it includes establishing prayer and patience over the difficulties that follow, because people deviate from the call, hold enmity toward the call, and turn away from it. The harms include both verbal harm and physical aggression. The trials include trials of wealth and trials of life.

"Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination" (Qur'an 31:17). The meaning of 'azm al-umur is this: when, after hesitation on the path, a person resolves upon a direction and then traverses the road. Now Luqman, having given his advice on beliefs and worship, moves it into the realm of ethics, which is the best provision for any caller (da'i) to Allah. This is because calling to Allah does not mean that a person should regard others as contemptible and himself as superior, and then, if he becomes powerful while calling, impose his leadership upon people. And if a person does not even do the work of calling to good, yet still acts great and remains above people, this is an exceedingly ugly conduct.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 18–19:

ولا تصعر خدک ۔۔۔۔۔ لصوت الحمیر (18 – 19) Ṣa'r is a disease that afflicts a camel, causing it to bend its neck sideways. The Qur'an, by likening the conduct of the arrogant person to ṣa'r, seeks to make people averse to it. The act of arrogance and aversion is called ṣa'r, meaning turning one's cheeks away from people out of pride and conceit. Walking on the earth with arrogance means walking with vanity and haughtiness. Being heedless and regarding people as nothing is a conduct that Allah also finds detestable, and people too consider it bad. Such a person holds a high opinion of himself and displays it in his gait.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every arrogant boaster.﴾ (31:18)

Alongside the prohibition of walking arrogantly, it is also made clear that one should walk with moderation.

﴿And be moderate in your pace.﴾ (31:19)

Qaṣd (moderation) means the middle course, that is, an economic policy free from extravagance, because a person who walks arrogantly, twisting his neck and considering himself superior, wastes his strength; it is, as it were, extravagance. Qaṣd may also mean intention, that is, that the movement of your walking should have a purpose and your destination should be fixed. And a person who walks with self-admiration has no aim other than show and greatness in his own mind, and that is no purpose at all; that is, if you walk, walk with a simple manner for a purpose. Lowness of voice contains courtesy. The person who speaks in it speaks with confidence and is certain of the truth of his words. A person who speaks in a loud, thundering voice is generally impolite, or does not believe in his own words, or wishes to conceal the weakness of his personality under noise and clamour. A liar always displays fervour and zeal. It is the Qur'an's own style that here, to show the evil of purposeless loud voice, it presents an extremely detestable, contemptible and foolish image.

﴿Indeed, the most hateful of voices is the braying of donkeys.﴾ (31:19)

Thus, by likening every loud voice to the braying of donkeys, it is made repugnant, and so every intelligent and well-mannered person comes to regard it as base and hateful. One who keeps this contemptuous image in his mind will never raise his voice like the braying of donkeys. Thus this second stage ends, within which the first matter has been discussed. This discussion has been carried out in a most varied and, from the most modern perspective, very fresh style, in the Qur'an's own manner of portrayal.

Lesson No. 186: Explanation of the Verses

20 ... to ... 34

This is the third round of this surah. It begins with a description of the cosmic evidence, which relates to people and to the facilities and benefits of their lives: the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them, both apparent and hidden, from which they benefit by night and by day. Yet despite these, they are not ashamed to dispute about the One who bestows these favours, the Bountiful, the Giver. After this, the same issue of Tawhid (Oneness of Allah) is presented, as it was in the two previous journeys.

﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and has completed upon you His favours, both apparent and hidden?﴾ (31:20 – 21)

This is a scene that we witness every day, and which the Qur'an repeatedly narrates. Each time, the panorama of the universe appears new to the reader, because this vast universe, whenever any of its aspects is considered, whenever its secrets are pondered over, and whenever its wonders are observed, appears new. Its secrets and wonders never end. Within his limited lifespan, a human being cannot acquire all the knowledge. Whenever a discovery is made, the intellect is astonished, and whenever we reflect afresh, we find it new.

Here the Qur'an presents this aspect of the universe: that Allah has made this universe subservient to us, and it fulfils human needs from every direction. Then, when all the things existing within this universe are analysed, its composition is very strange, which shows that it was made by a wise, planning engineer, and that it did not come into being by mere chance. Therefore it becomes evident that a will is working behind this entire universe, and that Allah is the Planner, who created man and placed all the things of the universe at his service, and then placed every thing of this earth at the service of man.

As for this awe-inspiring universe, this earth is a tiny particle of it, and upon this earth man is a small, weak creature, in comparison with the size of the earth and in comparison with the forces that Nature has placed within the earth, which are both living and dead. In comparison with these forces, man is nothing in terms of his size, strength and weight. But Allah has favoured man, breathed His spirit into his body, and given him preference over a large portion of His creation. It is this grace of Allah that has resulted in the requirement that this creature should have importance upon this earth, and that its status should be higher than all creatures. Within it should be the power and capacity to put the resources of this world to use, and within it should be the power and capacity to put the resources of this world to use and to search for its natural treasures. The subjugation indicated in this verse is precisely this, because the subjugation of the universe is itself counted among the apparent and hidden blessings of Allah. This subjugation is in addition to the fact that Allah has made the forces of the heavens beneficial for man. The very existence of man is a grace of Allah, and then man is given such power and capacity that he may subdue the rebellious forces of this universe. This is the second grace of Allah, and then the sending of Messengers for his guidance is a further grace of Allah. Every breath that he takes, every heartbeat that circulates blood in his body, every scene of this world that he sees, every sound that strikes his ears, every thought that comes into his conscience, and every new idea that he creates: all these are the blessings of Allah, a single one of which man cannot be thankful for throughout his entire life. All of these are nothing but the favours of Allah.

For this human creature, Allah has subjected all the forces that lie between the heavens and the earth. He has put the rays of the sun in his service, made the light of the moon beneficial for him, and provided him with guidance in the seas through the stars. Rain, wind, birds and animals have been shown to be beneficial to him. Whatever is within him has become beneficial and subservient for him. This we can see with great ease. Upon these we should reflect night and day. Upon this vast and wide earth he has been made a vicegerent, and control over all the treasures of the earth has been established for him. Some treasures are apparent and some are hidden. Some are such that their traces and effects lie within his perception. Some are beyond his perception as yet, and some are such that he has been benefiting from them while not even knowing of them. In short, every moment of the day and night, the rain of Allah's grace and bounty pours upon man, and he is immersed in the mercies of Allah, yet he does not know what the limit of these mercies is, or what their kinds and varieties are. Nevertheless, despite all these matters, there is a group among people which does not give thanks for these blessings of Allah, does not reflect upon them, and, by contemplating its surroundings, does not reach certainty.

﴿And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge, or guidance, or an illuminating Book.﴾ (31:20)

It is strange that such disputation about Allah should occur, while this universe and its variety lie before us, and we do not even know the number of these abundant blessings. In such circumstances, this denial and this rejection are extremely ugly, extremely blameworthy, detestable, and contrary to human nature. And if a person reflects, his hair stands on end out of fear, and it is clearly apparent that the one who denies the blessings of Allah is, in reality, naturally perverted. There has arisen a corruption within his nature. He is not hearing the call of the universe spread around him, and he has become so bold and shameless that he commits impudence against such a Benefactor. Moreover, this disputation and denial of such a person is based on no science whatsoever; it is based purely on ignorance. Further, such a person has neither a scriptural proof nor an illuminating argument.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verse 21:

﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا﴾ (31:21): "And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has sent down,' they say, 'No, we will follow that which we found our fathers upon.'" This is their only argument for their attitude. It is also a strange argument: a stone-like, rigid imitation (taqlid), based neither on knowledge nor on any sound view. This is precisely the taqlid from which Islam wants to free humanity. It grants their intellect the freedom to reflect independently, and it seeks to spread awakening, movement and light within the human being. But people have turned away from the traces of their past and have tied themselves like cattle to a pillar, and have put shackles on themselves.

Islam is, in reality, the name of the dignity of conscience and the dignity of consciousness. It moves forward in search of light. It is a system of life in which there is no imitation, no servitude and no rigidity. Yet, alas, these people deny it, cast this freedom away from their own souls, and argue about Allah without any guidance and without any illuminating Book. For this reason they are now being mocked, and the hidden peril of their position is pointed out to them.

﴿أَوَلَوْ كَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ يَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾ (31:21): "Would they follow them even if Satan were calling them to the punishment of the Blaze?" They have adopted this position on the invitation of Satan, so that he may lead them to the Fire of Hell. So the question is this: even if Satan is leading them towards Hell, will they still follow him? This is an extremely arresting rebuke, extremely awakening and frightening, especially after this great cosmic argument.

This stubborn ignorance and this argument are the subject of dispute. Now they are told what the proper course of conduct for them is, and what course they should adopt after this cosmic evidence and Allah's vast bounties.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 31, verse 22:

ومن یسلم ۔۔۔۔۔ واقبۃ الامور (22) ” “۔

That is, to submit one's whole being completely before Allah, and to adopt good deeds and good conduct along with it; that is, complete surrender and being fully content with Allah's decrees, being steeped in Allah's commands, guidance and obligations, with the awareness and conviction that Allah's mercy is with us and that Allah is watchful over us at all times. One's conscience finds the pleasure of Allah, and in this surrender one considers the whole universe, along with oneself, to be prostrating before Him. All these indications are contained in the phrase "surrendering one's face to Allah." The face is in fact the most honoured part of the human being.

ومن یسلم وجھہ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ بالعروۃ الوثقٰی (31: 22) "Whoever surrenders his face to Allah while doing good has indeed grasped the most trustworthy handhold." That is, the rope that does not break, that never becomes loose, and that does not deceive the one who holds it. The meaning is the support that a person grasps. Whoever submits himself to Allah should know that in the most difficult circumstances, in dark nights, in severe difficulties and in fierce storms, he will never be left without support.

This firm support is the conviction and the profound connection that exists between the believing servant and his Lord. Such a person is content in every condition, and whatever difficulties come upon him, he bears them with complete tranquillity and dignity. In great events and calamities he remains dignified and endures hardships. Moreover, if he is prosperous, he does not go beyond himself, and he lives his life with moderation and seriousness. Likewise, if a sudden crisis comes upon him, he does not lose his composure, nor is he distressed by the various difficulties that come in the way of God.

The journey of the Islamic call is long and full of dangers. In it, deprivations and difficulties are dangerous, but prosperity and wealth are even more dangerous. Calamity is a trial, and well-being is also a trial. Therefore, on this path there is constant need of a support that never loosens, a rope that does not snap, and this need remains at all times. That is, the need for a firm support. And what is this firm support? Embracing Islam, believing in Allah, surrendering to Him, and adopting the path of ihsan (excellence). Then one hands over the outcome to Allah.

وال اللہ عاقبۃ الامور (31: 22) "And to Allah belongs the final outcome of affairs." That is, the return is to Him and He is the ultimate refuge. So it is fitting that a person surrenders himself to Him in advance, and keeps travelling toward Him with clear confidence and in accordance with the guidance of the Qur'an and Sunnah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 23–24:

ومن کفر فلا ۔۔۔۔ عذاب غلیظ (23 – 24) ”۔“

That was the end of those who fully surrender themselves to Allah, and this is the end of those who refuse to adopt disbelief.

ومن کفر فلا یحزنک کفرہ (31: 23) "And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you." It is not fitting that they should cause worry to you, you who are the master of both worlds. They are very insignificant and small, and their end in the Hereafter will be even more contemptible. They are in Allah's grip; they cannot escape from Allah. Allah will seize them for their deeds; He knows well the deeds of every person, whether they are apparent or hidden, whether they are in the breast or in the intention.

الینا مرجعھم ۔۔۔۔۔ بذات الصدور (31: 23) "To Us is their return. Then We will inform them of what they have done. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts." The provision of life that deceives a person is for a brief period and is of very little value.

نمتعھم قلیلا ۔۔۔۔۔ عذاب غلیظ (31: 24) "We will let them enjoy themselves for a little while, then We will drive them, helpless, toward a severe punishment." They will enjoy themselves for a few days, then they will encounter a terrifying punishment, and they will be pushed and dragged toward that punishment. The word ghaliz is used in describing the punishment, and through it the punishment is given a concrete form. And in the sense of compulsion (iḍṭirār), the helplessness of the disbelievers is expressed, meaning they will be unable to save themselves from that punishment and will not be able to delay or evade it. This was the condition of the disbelievers. But whoever firmly grasps the rope of Allah, submits his face entirely to Allah, and sets out toward his Lord with seriousness and tranquility, will be in a far more exalted station compared to the disbeliever.

Now they are confronted with the logical proof of their own nature, when this great universe is placed before them and the question is posed whether it has a creator or not. Obviously, they can say nothing but that Allah exists, because the Divine Being is part of human nature. No other interpretation of this universe can be made. Yet these people deviate even from this simple logic of nature and forget it, although there is no other stronger and correct proof than this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 25–26:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ ... ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (25–26)

Any sensible person, when he asks his own heart who the Creator of this great universe is, will find the same answer: Allah. Every person finds this answer within his own nature. This earth and these heavens stand before our eyes; their conditions, their sizes, their movements, their distances, their properties and their attributes are all measured, precise, definite, and strung together in mutual order and arrangement. Moreover, they are created things, and no claimant exists who says that he is their creator. Nor can anyone claim that there is a creator of them other than Allah. Nor is it rationally possible that this great universe came into being by itself, just like that. Furthermore, it is also not possible that there is no need for a manager (mudabbir). Whoever holds that it came into existence by itself, established itself by itself, and became orderly by itself, merely by chance, is none other than the greatest fool. Such a statement is rejected by the depths of human nature.

Those who, in that era, were opposing the belief in tawhid (Oneness of God) and standing in the way of the Prophet's ﷺ call were engaged in fierce disputation. These people could not withstand the awareness and logic of their own nature when this universe and its existence were placed before them, which was visible before their eyes and only required looking. Therefore, they did not hesitate in answering this question. When they were asked, "Who created the earth and the heavens?", they would immediately say, "Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was instructed that in response to this answer he should simply praise Allah: ﴿Al-hamdu lillah﴾ (All praise is for Allah). All praise is for Allah, that the truth had become clear to them and they had accepted the natural logic. Thanks be to Allah that they had become monotheists at least to the extent of the creation of this universe. Continue to praise and glorify Him in every state beyond this. Now, leaving aside argument and debate, here is another observation.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ (31:25). This is why they engage in argument and dispute. They do not understand the signs of nature, and despite the existence of this great universe, they do not believe in the doctrine of tawhid. Since they have accepted the Oneness of Allah only to the extent of the creation of the earth and the heavens, it is now told that Allah, being the Creator, is also the absolute Owner of this universe, both of the portion that has been made subservient to man and of the portion that has not been made subservient. Yet He is free of need from the earth, the heavens, and all creation between them, and He is Praiseworthy in His own essence, even if people do not praise Him.

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ (31:26). This discourse now concludes with the statement that Allah's self-sufficiency has no end. His knowledge is unlimited, His power is boundless, and nothing stands as an obstacle before His will. He is capable over all creation, and this fact is conveyed in the form of a cosmic scene.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 25–26:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ ... ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (25–26)

Any sensible person, when he asks his own heart who the Creator of this great universe is, will find the same answer: Allah. Every person finds this answer within his own nature. This earth and these heavens stand before our eyes; their conditions, their sizes, their movements, their distances, their properties and their attributes are all measured, precise, definite, and strung together in mutual order and arrangement. Moreover, they are created things, and no claimant exists who says that he is their creator. Nor can anyone claim that there is a creator of them other than Allah. Nor is it rationally possible that this great universe came into being by itself, just like that. Furthermore, it is also not possible that there is no need for a manager (mudabbir). Whoever holds that it came into existence by itself, established itself by itself, and became orderly by itself, merely by chance, is none other than the greatest fool. Such a statement is rejected by the depths of human nature.

Those who, in that era, were opposing the belief in tawhid (Oneness of God) and standing in the way of the Prophet's ﷺ call were engaged in fierce disputation. These people could not withstand the awareness and logic of their own nature when this universe and its existence were placed before them, which was visible before their eyes and only required looking. Therefore, they did not hesitate in answering this question. When they were asked, "Who created the earth and the heavens?", they would immediately say, "Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was instructed that in response to this answer he should simply praise Allah: ﴿Al-hamdu lillah﴾ (All praise is for Allah). All praise is for Allah, that the truth had become clear to them and they had accepted the natural logic. Thanks be to Allah that they had become monotheists at least to the extent of the creation of this universe. Continue to praise and glorify Him in every state beyond this. Now, leaving aside argument and debate, here is another observation.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ (31:25). This is why they engage in argument and dispute. They do not understand the signs of nature, and despite the existence of this great universe, they do not believe in the doctrine of tawhid. Since they have accepted the Oneness of Allah only to the extent of the creation of the earth and the heavens, it is now told that Allah, being the Creator, is also the absolute Owner of this universe, both of the portion that has been made subservient to man and of the portion that has not been made subservient. Yet He is free of need from the earth, the heavens, and all creation between them, and He is Praiseworthy in His own essence, even if people do not praise Him.

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ (31:26). This discourse now concludes with the statement that Allah's self-sufficiency has no end. His knowledge is unlimited, His power is boundless, and nothing stands as an obstacle before His will. He is capable over all creation, and this fact is conveyed in the form of a cosmic scene.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 27–28:

ولو ان ما فی الارض ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ ان اللہ سمیع بصیر (27 – 28)

This is a scene drawn from human knowledge and limited observation, so that the boundless works of Allah's will may be brought close to human imagination. Without this figurative and embodied manner, human imagination could not grasp it at all.

Human beings write down their knowledge, record their sayings, enforce their decrees, and write with pens. These pens they make from reeds and from wood, and then, having cut them, they write with them. This ink is kept in a bottle or an inkwell. Thus it is said: even if all the trees of the earth were made into pens, and the waters of all the seas were turned into ink, and seven more seas like them were brought, and the writers sat down to write, the new words of Allah which indicate His knowledge would not be exhausted; all those seas' ink would run out, while the words of Allah's knowledge would not end, and the limit of Allah's knowledge would not be reached. This is because a limited power seeks to encompass the unlimited. However far a limited power goes, its strength ends at some point, while the unlimited remains unlimited and beyond encompassing. In short, the words of Allah do not end, because Allah's knowledge is unlimited. Allah's will does not stop at any boundary, and there are no limits or restrictions upon Allah's will.

Trees and seas vanish. All living things and all dead things vanish and come to an end. All conditions and forms pass behind the veil, and the human heart remains awed before Allah's majesty and power. That power which neither moves, nor changes, nor disappears. Before the Creator, the Mighty, the Governor, the Wise, a human being is left astonished.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ (31:27). In this journey we stand before a terrifying scene, and now comes the final plucking of the strings of human thought and perception: it is declared that for Allah, the resurrection of all people is very easy.

﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ (31:28). That is, the creation of all of you and your revival after death is, for Allah, no different from creating and raising a single soul. That will which, upon turning toward something, brings creation into being, is indifferent whether it turns toward one thing or toward countless things. For Allah it is not the case that He fashions each person one by one and labours over each individual. For Him, creating one person and creating countless millions of people are of the same kind. Raising one person to life and raising countless billions is, for Allah, one and the same. Allah need only say the single word "Kun" (Be).

﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. With this power, this knowledge, and this skill, creation, resurrection after death, and the reckoning will be carried out. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (31:28).

Now this surah has a third journey, or third round. In it too the same question of tawhid is under discussion that was in the first two journeys. The verdict is given that Allah is the Truth, that those partners whom people call upon are false, and that worship is due to Allah alone. In the reckoning that will follow the Day of Judgment, a father will be unable to ransom his child, nor will a child be able to repay anything on behalf of his parents. Alongside these verdicts, several other contemporary issues are taken up in a highly effective manner. All these matters too are discussed within the framework of this universe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 29–30:

﴿Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter into the day, and causes the day to enter into the night...﴾ (29–30)

The night entering into the day and the day entering into the night, their being opposite to one another, and their lengthening and shortening across the different seasons, is a wondrous sight. But seeing it year after year, and its recurring again and again, makes people familiar with it, and the majority, even while beholding this marvel, do not truly perceive it. Yet it occurs with the utmost precision and under a rigid order, and not even a second's difference enters into it. No disturbance ever comes into it, not even once. This continuous rotation of the earth and the orbiting of the celestial bodies, in which no sphere deviates from its orbit or fails to keep to it, is a great marvel. Only the Being of Allah, alone, is able to bring into existence, run, and safely maintain such a system. This reality is grasped only through observing the heavenly firmaments and the orbits of the celestial spheres.

The change of night and day is also evident from the revolution of the sun and the moon. Subjecting the sun and the moon and keeping them suspended in space is even more wondrous than the occurrence of day and night, and more wondrous than their lengthening and shortening. Only Allah, who is the Governor and the All-Aware, can subject this great system, and it is He who can keep these things running with accurate measure until a appointed time. The night entering into the day and the day entering into the night is merely a small part of this entire universe. The subjugation of the sun and the moon is also a clear reality. The significance of the sun and the moon for an ordinary person is that these two celestial bodies are before him and near him; otherwise, in the universe, they too are mere specks, insignificant specks. After this great knowledge and arrangement, then:

﴿Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ (31:29). This is a simple matter. After these cosmic realities, this unseen reality is very small, and for Allah its doing is not difficult. These two realities are interconnected. After the three realities, namely the turning of night and day, the subjugation of the sun and the moon, and Allah's being All-Knowing and All-Aware, a great reality is stated on which these three realities depend, and this great reality is expressed in this context and this argument is given for it:

﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ (31:30). "That," that is, this cosmic system, which is very intricate, precise, enduring, stable, and extremely harmonious. This system is established because Allah is the Truth, and all other deities besides Allah are falsehood. This cosmic system stands by the Supreme Truth, and the Supreme Truth is Allah, the Necessarily Existent, by whom this whole existence stands. Since this universe stands, Allah is the Truth, and it is for this reason that this universe stands. It is He who establishes it, sustains it, protects it, and manages it. He is the guarantee of the universe's continuance, and He is the cause of its stability, connection, and order.

﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ (31:30). Everything other than Allah is changing and transforming. Everything other than Allah turns its direction. Everything other than Allah undergoes increase and decrease. Weakness and strength, youth and old age, rise and fall, prosperity and adversity come upon it. Everything other than Allah neither was, nor came to be, nor will be [in the sense of eternal permanence]. It is Allah alone who is eternal and everlasting, and upon Him no change, transformation, or decline comes. Within the human soul there remains something, and that is the full meaning of Allah's saying:

﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ (31:30). We have not been able to transfer its full meaning into words. It has a meaning and it is felt, but for me it is difficult to bring it into words. Likewise, this expression: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ (31:30), there is no Most High and Great except Him. Regarding these expressions, I have said something which my entire being finds. I say that human expressions do not have words through which the realities contained in these two phrases can be expressed. These are very lofty realities. Allah is the Truth, the Most High, the Great. Human expressions confine the meanings that can be perceived from these phrases. Therefore, only the Qur'anic expression is sufficient for them.

After this cosmic scene, this scene of the higher realm, there is another scene which keeps coming within human experience and observation: the days and nights through which human beings pass. It is a ship sailing across the vast expanse of the sea. This too sails by the grace and bounty of Allah. Allah places people in this scene in a dangerous condition. Many of those addressed have themselves passed through such scenes. It is a natural journey in which a person is surrounded by nature and natural forces. He has no power, no resistance, no grip, and no pride. When a person is traveling in that ship and is in the depths of the sea...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verses 31–32:

Alam tara annal-fulka ... kullu khattarin kafur (31–32)

This ship sails according to the laws of nature that Allah has placed in the sea, the ship, the wind, the earth and the heavens. Allah created these things with such properties that the ship began to move on the seas: it does not sink, and it does not remain fixed in one place. If any one of these properties were to be lost in any one of these things, the ship could not move in the sea. If the density of the water were to disappear, or the density of the ship's material, or if its quantity were to increase or decrease. If the pressure of the air over the sea were to decrease, or if there were a disturbance in the waves of the wind or the waves of the sea, and if the temperature disappeared, by which water remains water and by which the waves of the air and water remain within their proper limits. If even a one percent change occurred from the present state, the ship would not be able to float upon the waters of the sea. Apart from these properties, when compared with other factors, Allah becomes the supporter and helper of the ship, in that He restrains the rebelliousness of the waves. He protects it from storms and weather effects. In the depths of the sea there is no one else to save, except Allah; therefore it moves in every condition with the mercy, kindness, grace and favour of Allah. Then, within it are loaded the things of Allah's bounty. The Qur'an shows that the word "fadl" (bounty) can have both of these meanings.

Liyurikum min ayatihi (31:31): "So that He may show you His signs, which are before your eyes, provided someone wishes to see. There is in them no ambiguity or concealment."

Inna fi dhalika ... shakur (31:31): "Indeed, in that are signs for every patient and grateful person." That is, one who is patient upon difficulties and grateful upon ease. A person is always in one of these two states. But the condition of people is that they neither act patiently nor give thanks. When a calamity comes, they begin to shriek, and if deliverance is granted, only a few of them show gratitude.

Wa idha ghashiyahum ... lahud-din (31:32): "And when a wave covers them like a canopy, they call upon Allah, making their religion sincerely His alone." In such conditions, when the ship is like a straw upon the deep seas and the waves rise like canopies and come over the ship, in such dangerous circumstances these people, abandoning false gods and imaginary deities, call upon Allah alone. In the days of peace and security, these false and imaginary objects of worship cover their nature and come between their nature and the Creator of nature; and in the state of peril, when these veils fall, their nature is revealed uncovered beneath the veils and layers, and it stands upright before its Lord. It turns back to its Lord, and then it makes the religion sincerely for Allah. Now it rejects every false claimant, abandons every deity that is alien, and, making the religion sincerely for Allah, calls upon Him alone.

Falamma najjahum ilal-bari famnhum muqtasid (31:32): "Then, when He delivers them safely to the land, some of them observe moderation." It does not drag them into peace and security, prosperity, rebellion and transgression. And they continue constantly to give thanks to Allah. Although such a person does not fully discharge Allah's right in remembrance and reflection, because the furthest a person who remembers and gives thanks can reach is to be moderate in performance and upright in the truth. (Therefore, "muqtasid" means one who practises moderation.) Some people are such that as soon as the danger passes and the state of safety comes, they deny the signs of Allah.

Wa ma yajhadu bi-ayatina illa kullu khattarin kafur (31:32): "And none denies Our signs except every treacherous and ungrateful person." Khattar means one who is extremely treacherous, and kafur means one who commits intense disbelief. This hyperbolic form becomes a quality of a person, and these words are most fitting for one who, even on seeing these incomparable signs of the universe and even on encountering the clear logic of nature, denies the signs of Allah.

In keeping with the terrors of the sea, where people's pride in knowledge, pride in strength and pride in power are dispelled, and the veils of falsehood are removed from over nature, and a person finds the natural proofs and signs before him, in keeping with those terrors it is here made known that the real day of horrors will be the Day of Resurrection. Compared with that, the horrors of the sea are never anything at all. It will be such a terrifying day that the bond of father and son, the bond of kinship and the bond of blood will also come to an end. A parent will abandon his child, and a son will be fleeing from his parents; there every person will stand alone. There will be no helper and no support. All relationships and connections will come to an end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verse 33:

يٰۤاَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوْا ... وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللّٰهِ الْغَرُورُ (33). This will be a scene of every person being concerned only for himself. The fear that exists here in the world, in hearts and in consciousness, has only a semblance of it. But this fear of the Day of Judgment will be unparalleled. In it, all ties of kinship and blood will be severed. A mother will be fleeing from her child, and a child will have no concern or care for its parents. Every person will be concerned only with himself; it will be a state of every man for himself. No one will stand surety for another, and no one's deeds will benefit anyone except his own. Such circumstances, clearly, will be a terror for which there is no parallel in this world. Therefore, calling people here to fear God is a most fitting call, and the matter of the Hereafter is presented in a state of extreme fear, so minds and hearts are turned toward it.

إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللّٰهِ حَقٌّ (31:33): "Indeed, the promise of God is true." In reality, God's promise is true. God does not go against it, and God's word cannot be averted. Every person will pass through this unparalleled terror, and every person will have to render an account in full detail and hear a just judgment, as a result of which neither will a father be substituted for his son, nor a son for his father.

فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَيٰوةُ الدُّنْيَا (31:33): "So let not the life of this world deceive you." In this world there are provisions and amusements and play, but its respite is very limited. Here, man has been sent for a test.

وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللّٰهِ الْغَرُورُ (31:33): "And let not the deceiver deceive you concerning God." Let no provision deceive you. Let no entertainment lead you astray; let no Satan put you into doubt. Deceivers are many, Satans are countless, and the attractions of the world are on every side, drawing you in. The pride of wealth is also a Satan; the pride of knowledge is also a Satan; the pride of power is also a Satan, and worship of Satan is also a Satan; the desire of the self is also a Satan; bodily lust is also a Satan. The power that protects from all these Satans is the power of the fear of God.

At the close of this surah and at the end of this fourth round, and in keeping with this terrifying scene of the Hereafter, this final and somewhat sharper plectrum is struck upon the strings of thought and reason. In it is drawn the picture of God's boundless knowledge and man's limited knowledge: man's knowledge, from whose reach everything beyond the sight is hidden. Now the matter that is the subject of this surah is decided, and this conclusion emerges from the wondrous portrayal of the Qur'an: the picture of God's eternal and everlasting knowledge.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 31, verse 34:

﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour...﴾ ... ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ (34)

Allah has kept the moment of the Resurrection a hidden matter (ghayb) whose knowledge no one possesses, so that people remain alert at all times. They should always expect the Resurrection and always strive to earn provision for it. They do not know when the Resurrection will occur. In any case, it will come suddenly, and at that time no opportunity for preparation will be given, nor will there be permission to gather provisions.

Allah sends rain wherever He wills in accordance with His wisdom, and as much as He wills. People estimate the approach of rain through their experiences and instruments and signs. But they can neither create the causes for sending rain nor do they possess knowledge of the time. The verse only states that Allah sends the rain, because it is Allah who provides the natural causes for rain and organizes them. Allah's exclusivity in rain is that He alone has the power to send it down, as is apparent from the outward meaning of the verse. Those who have placed the time of rain within the particular unseen knowledge of Allah have not been correct in this view, although knowledge truly belongs to Allah alone, and it is exclusive to Him in every matter, because Allah's knowledge alone is correct, lasting and all-encompassing, and there is no deficiency or excess in it.

﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾ (31:34): "He alone knows what is being nurtured in the wombs of mothers." This is a particular knowledge of the same kind as the knowledge of the Hour, and no one except Allah knows what is in a mother's womb. That is, what is being nurtured inside the womb at every moment and every instant. Especially since the pregnancy has no weight or volume at that time. Whether the child in the womb is male or female, from the initial time when the cell enters the egg, Allah knows what its features are, what its characteristics are, what its condition and capacity are. All these matters are exclusive to Allah's knowledge.

﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ (31:34): whether it will earn good or evil, whether it will gain benefit or loss, whether it will face ease or difficulty, whether it will remain healthy or fall ill, whether it will obey Allah or disobey Him. This is because earning (kasb) is far more general than mere profit. Earning includes all the circumstances that may befall a person. This is an unseen matter whose doors are closed. It lies behind veils, and man stands behind the veils and does not know what lies ahead.

﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ (31:34): because this too is a matter that lies behind the veil of tomorrow, and a thick veil of the future stands between it and the human soul. The human soul stands on this side of those veils. It is helpless and knows not what will happen in the next moment. From this it becomes evident how limited human knowledge is and how clear its helplessness is. By reflecting in this way, pride in knowledge and understanding is removed from his mind, and thus it becomes known to them that man has been given very little knowledge, and that behind the veil of tomorrow there are countless matters which man does not know. If man knew all the things on this side of those veils, he would stand at those veils and try to find out what tomorrow would bring. But man does not know what tomorrow will bring; rather, he does not know what will happen in the next moment. Thus the human soul comes down a little from its arrogance. It fears Allah and prays: O Allah, let there be good in the next moment.

The Qur'an presents this particular knowledge of Allah within a very wide scope, a scope that has a great and profound effect on man. This field encompasses the breadth of time and place. The present is within its grasp, and so is the coming future; the near and the far; the thoughts of hearts, and whisperings and anxieties; the hour of the Resurrection and also the times of rain. Then this field extends to the wombs of mothers, which are hidden from sight. Then behind the veil lies the near future, namely what will happen tomorrow. Though time is near, knowledge lies in the distant valleys of ignorance. This circle extends up to death and the grave.

In sum, Allah's particular knowledge has a vast circle. But the Qur'an's manner of expression has gathered the edges of this vast cloak and collected it into the form of a bundle. This is the vast cloak of the unseen, and within it all matters of diverse kinds have been placed and gathered together. Now all these matters are particular, specific matters, and this bundle is firmly tied. Nothing the size of the eye of a needle can come out of it. The door to this knowledge is closed before man, because this sphere of power lies beyond man. It lies beyond human knowledge, and no one knows it except Allah. Yes, if Allah by His command informs someone of something, that is a different matter. Allah is Knowing and Acquainted, and there is no knower and acquainted other than Him.

Here this Surah ends. In truth, it was a long and distant journey. Now we return, tired from this distant journey of contemplation. We traversed long roads, bore burdens, and reflected. We observed the manifestations of Allah's power in this universe, the world and its varied birds and animals. This Surah consists of 34 verses, but the world of meanings and thoughts is vast and broad, and very blessed. Blessed is the Being who created the heart and the mind, who sent down this Qur'an, which is a healing for diseases of the heart and a guidance and mercy for the believers.
